not sure if this is a language barrier or not, but what is there to debate about? Each player only getting 1 reaction per turn (resets at the beginning of their turn) is the standard rule. Page 8 of the starter kit rulebook: 

Reactions are specific things you can do as the result

of some trigger event happening. You can Defend as

a Reaction (as described in Hit the Deck) and some

abilities give you the option for other Reactions; the

ability’s description has all the pertinent details. No

matter how many Reaction abilities you have, you can

only perform one Reaction a round, resetting at the start

of your turn. So, if you use your Reaction during your

turn, you won’t get another until the start of your next

turn.

posts.name: VGBM
posts.cooked:
I think there's some slight confusion here about the difference between a turn and a round. When Anubis says one reaction per turn, he means when someone activates a reaction, no one else can react until the turn is passed to a different actor. And the current known rule is one reaction per character per round.

A better way to word it would be the way it is in the op, which is whether there should be a rule against reacting to reactions. And I agree with Jester that that seems unnecessary. Though any dm could make a house rule about that if they want.

I ruling I got (form Dave) was you can not react to a reaction.

In the game every player get a reaction, it refreshed at the start of their turn.

 

So in turn 1 you go first, it does not refesh until you go next, even if you are the last person in turn 2.

I hope that clears it up.

posts.name: Bigbywolfe
posts.cooked:
You don't get 1 Reaction per game, you get 1 Reaction every Round, that will often (usually) take place when it is not your turn. As the rules are currently presented in the Starter Kit nothing prevents one character's Reaction from triggering another character's Reaction. If that is really their intent they better spell it out clearly, since there is no logical reason to not let it happen. 

Also, it would be nice if you could link us to Dave's ruling (or copy/paste it) so we have the exact wording of his answer.
